tool.name: ExtractTrainingSamples

param.name: training_samples
param.dialogReference: Feature layer containing training samples (points or polygons). For polygon samples, values are extracted from all pixels within each polygon. For point samples, values are extracted at the exact point location. Ensure samples include a field identifying the landcover class.

param.name: input_raster
param.dialogReference: Multi-band raster dataset from which to extract values. Each band becomes a column in the output table. This is typically the same raster used for model training, but can be any raster covering the training sample locations.

param.name: output_table
param.dialogReference:
Output table containing extracted raster values and class labels. The table includes:

  • One column per raster band (named Band_1, Band_2, etc.)

  • Class value column

  • Coordinate columns (for point samples)

  • Format can be CSV (.csv) or Excel (.xlsx), depending on the file extension specified.

tool.summary:
Extract raster values at training sample locations to create a tabular dataset for external analysis. It is useful for

  • Exploratory data analysis

  • Custom model training in external software

  • Statistical analysis of class separability

  • Quality checking training data

For polygon samples, the tool extracts values from all pixels within each polygon. For point samples, it extracts values at exact point locations.
tool.usage:
Use this tool to:

  • Export training data for analysis in R, Python, or other software

  • Check for class overlap or confusion in feature space

  • Identify potentially mislabeled samples

  • Create datasets for custom modelling workflows

The output table contains one row per sample (points) or per pixel (polygons), with columns for each raster band plus class information.
